mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
regime_hint: dual inflation and rate hike cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) over the past six months indicates a rebalancing toward consumption, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, RSAFS) > 0.6 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST and RSAFS are strongly positively correlated over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below the long-run average growth rate, without a concurrent decline in unemployment, signals structural demand weakness that is not offset by labor market strength, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < long-run average AND UNRATE not > 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 grows below its long-run average and unemployment remains below 5%.
